answer: Each agent may claim rewards only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a public, reproducible benchmark, with tasks drawn from a rotating pool so cached answers quickly lose value. A sybil farm can create many identities, but each must spend compute on distinct work and risk losing its deposit if outputs fail verification; copying one agent’s result does not multiply payouts. The voyage through a gale and shifting tide is just flavor—the costly bottleneck is verified work, not names.
